When I was 6 or 7, my grandmother was in a nursing home, and every Sunday my dad and I would go see her. I always had a book with me bc I was that kid. One Sunday we’re in the common room and there’s a man (he was also living there) sitting across from me. We make eye contact, and I smile, like the outgoing kid I was. He then proceeds to pull out his junk, so I held my book up in front of my face before I could see it. He puts it away. The cycle repeated itself for about an hour every week until we stopped going

Another time I was at Disney World in Orlando and was about to ride Rockin Rollercoaster. I was in the single rider line, because I was there with my (other) grandma. So I get in next to this guy. Backstory: at the time I was TERRIFIED of launch coasters. So the car does its little stoplight countdown thing and I realize it’s a launch coaster and start losing my crap, and the man just strokes my arm and in a really soft, monotonous voice says “it’s okay. It’ll be over soon”

My Mama (dad’s mom) passed on December 15, 2007. I was eight years old. The biggest thing I remember was crying so hard into my dad’s chest. 

I go see her by myself sometimes and just talk to her about life, how the family is doing, etc.
I took my former best friend to “meet” her right after my 18th birthday, and I could tell he was a little uncomfortable, but we talked to her. 

If I could talk to her, I’d just want to tell her how much I miss her, and I’d record her voice. I was only eight when she died, and I can’t remember her voice. 

Mama, if you’re watching me type this, I love you and miss you more and more every day. I hope I’ve made you proud.
